newsitem.title: CHINA: GITIC ratings to reflect changing role - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: GITIC ratings to reflect changing role - Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday its ratings assessments for Guangdong International Trust and Investment (GITIC) will reflect the risks associated with a distancing from its owner, China's Guangdong province.
GITIC was formed to source foreign financial investment, technology, management expertise and skills for Guangdong province.
But Moody's said the opening of the province to outside investors, especially through Hong Kong, now gives borrowers greater ability to access foreign funds directly, eroding GITIC's influence.

Moody's said "in common with other non-bank financial institutions in China, provision of emergency support for GITIC is increasingly likely to be limited to that provided by the province" as China's central authorities distance themselves from the support of such institutions.
Moody's rates GITIC's long-term senior debt at Baa2.
